description.summary: surfaces in the compositor's menu bar

protocol.description:
The menu bar is a strip the compositor owns on each output, as WindowServer does on macOS: its geometry, its tone over the wallpaper, auto-hide and the reveal in full screen are decided there. What sits in it comes from clients, each drawing its own part:
- an app's menu titles (the system menu, the app's name, its menus) on a menu-titles surface, shown only while that app is frontmost. Its last committed buffer stays on screen when the app stops answering, while opening a menu needs the app; - status items, each on its own surface, which the compositor lines up from the right: the system items (from Control Center) first in their order, then the apps' items, newest leftmost.
Input in these surfaces goes to their owners, which open their menus and popovers as their own xdg_popups attached with get_popup. The surfaces have no xdg role; their size is that of their buffer, and they get the strip's height in configure.

description.summary: gives surfaces a place in the menu bar

request.name: destroy
request.description: The objects made through it stay valid.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the surface already has a role

entry.name: app
entry.summary: an app's item, left of the system items

request.name: get_menu_titles

description.summary: the surface of the client's menu titles

request.description: The surface shows at the start of the strip while the client is the frontmost app. A client has one at a time; a second one replaces the first.

request.name: get_status_item
request.description: System items are ordered by order, 0 rightmost; app items by creation.

arg.name: order
arg.summary: among the system items, from the right

description.summary: an app's menu titles in the menu bar
remove the titles from the strip

event.name: configure
event.description: Sent on creation and when the strip or the room changes. The client draws a buffer at most width wide and exactly height tall, then acks.

arg.name: width
arg.summary: room before the status items, in logical pixels

arg.name: height
arg.summary: the strip's height, in logical pixels

event.name: shown

description.summary: the titles are on screen or not

event.description: Shown while the client is frontmost and the strip is visible.

request.name: get_popup

description.summary: attach a popup to the titles

request.description: The popup was made with a null parent; it is positioned against this surface.

entry.name: hide
entry.summary: Hide: the client's windows leave the screen

entry.name: hide_others
entry.summary: Hide Others: every other app's do

entry.name: show_all
entry.summary: Show All: every hidden app comes back

entry.name: bring_all_to_front
entry.summary: Bring All to Front: the client's windows come forward in their order

request.name: app_action

description.summary: run an item of the app menu that the compositor owns

request.description: Hide Others and Show All act on other apps, and hiding or raising the client's own windows changes the stacking and the focus: the compositor runs them, as it does for its own shortcuts. Only while the titles are shown (the client is frontmost); otherwise the request is ignored.

description.summary: a status item in the menu bar
remove the item from the strip

event.name: configure
event.description: The client draws a buffer exactly height tall, as wide as the item, then acks.

request.name: set_visible
request.description: A hidden item leaves no gap. Items start visible.

description.summary: attach a popup to the item
